category_title: Students with learning disabilities who use abbreviations and pre-quizzes to prioritize lecture content
student_description: Noah is a 7th-grade student with a learning disability who struggles with the temporal and cognitive demands of fast-paced lectures, often failing to capture any critical points on blank paper. He thrives when provided with explicit structural scaffolds, such as pre-lecture priming, structured note-taking templates, and strategies that allow him to write faster using abbreviations.

criteria.rationale: To manage the temporal demands of fast lectures, Noah must learn to reduce his writing volume so he can keep up.
criteria.check: The tutor's long-term plan includes teaching Noah specific strategies to write fewer words, such as creating personal abbreviations or omitting small words/articles.

criteria.rationale: Noah cannot immediately apply note-taking strategies at full lecture speed and needs structured practice to acclimate.
criteria.check: The tutor's long-term plan incorporates explicit modeling and guided practice with recorded or paced materials to help Noah gradually adjust to real-time lecture speeds.
